title.en: Biographies of Bian Que and the Duke of Cang
title.raw: 《扁鵲倉公列傳》 Biographies of Bian Que and the Duke of Cang

sentences.zh: 扁鵲者，勃海郡鄭人也，姓秦氏，名越人。

translations.literal: Bian Que was from Zheng in Bohai commandery, surname Qin, given name Yue Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Que was a native of Zheng in the Commandery of Bohai. His surname was Qin, and his given name was Yueren.

sentences.zh: 少時為人舍長。

translations.literal: In his youth he served as a lodging house manager.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth, he served as the manager of a guesthouse.

sentences.zh: 舍客長桑君過，扁鵲獨奇之，常謹遇之。

translations.literal: A guest at the lodging, Elder Sang, passed through. Bian Que alone found him extraordinary and constantly treated him with respect.
translations.idiomatic: A guest named Lord Changsang once stayed at the lodging house. Bian Que alone recognized something extraordinary about him and always treated him with the utmost courtesy.

sentences.zh: 長桑君亦知扁鵲非常人也。

translations.literal: Elder Sang also knew Bian Que was no ordinary person.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Changsang, for his part, also recognized that Bian Que was no ordinary man.

sentences.zh: 出入十餘年，乃呼扁鵲私坐，閒與語曰：「我有禁方，年老，欲傳與公，公毋泄。」

translations.literal: After coming and going for more than ten years, he called Bian Que to sit with him privately and said casually: "I have secret prescriptions. I am old and wish to pass them on to you; do not reveal them."
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years of visits, he summoned Bian Que to sit with him in private and said in an easy tone: "I have secret prescriptions. I am old now and wish to transmit them to you—you must not disclose them."

sentences.zh: 扁鵲曰：「敬諾。」

translations.literal: Bian Que said: "Respectful promise."
translations.idiomatic: Bian Que said: "I respectfully accept."

sentences.zh: 乃出其懷中藥予扁鵲：「飲是以上池之水，三十日當知物矣。」

translations.literal: Then exit his bosom middle medicine give Bian Que: "Drink this with shang pool water, thirty days should know things."
translations.idiomatic: Then he took medicine from his bosom and gave it to Bian Que: "Drink this with water from an upper pond, after thirty days you will perceive things."

sentences.zh: 乃悉取其禁方書盡與扁鵲。

translations.literal: Then he took all his secret prescription books and gave them all to Bian Que.
translations.idiomatic: He then took out all of his secret medical texts and gave every last one of them to Bian Que.

sentences.zh: 忽然不見，殆非人也。

translations.literal: He suddenly disappeared, probably not a mortal.
translations.idiomatic: Then he vanished without a trace—he was likely not a mortal being.

sentences.zh: 扁鵲以其言飲藥三十日，視見垣一方人。

translations.literal: Bian Que followed his words and drank the medicine for thirty days, then could see through walls to the people on the other side.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Que followed his instructions and drank the medicine for thirty days, after which he could see the people on the other side of a wall.

sentences.zh: 以此視病，盡見五藏癥結，特以診脈為名耳。

translations.literal: Using this to examine illnesses, he could see all the blockages in the five viscera, but used pulse diagnosis as his official name.
translations.idiomatic: He used this ability to examine the sick, perceiving every obstruction within the five organs, though he employed pulse diagnosis merely as a cover for his true method.

sentences.zh: 為醫或在齊，或在趙。

translations.literal: As a physician he practiced either in Qi or in Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He practiced medicine sometimes in Qi and sometimes in Zhao.

sentences.zh: 在趙者名扁鵲。

translations.literal: In Zhao he was called Bian Que.
translations.idiomatic: When he was in Zhao, he went by the name Bian Que.

sentences.zh: 當晉昭公時，諸大夫彊而公族弱，趙簡子為大夫，專國事。

translations.literal: During the time of Duke Zhao of Jin, the various ministers were strong while the ducal clan was weak. Zhao Jianzi served as minister and monopolized state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Duke Zhao of Jin, the great ministers had grown powerful while the ducal house had weakened. Zhao Jianzi, who served as a minister, had taken sole command of the affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 簡子疾，五日不知人，大夫皆懼，於是召扁鵲。

translations.literal: Jianzi fell ill, for five days unconscious. All the ministers were afraid, so they summoned Bian Que.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzi fell gravely ill and lay unconscious for five days. The other ministers grew alarmed, and so they summoned Bian Que.

sentences.zh: 扁鵲入視病，出，董安于問扁鵲，扁鵲曰：「血脈治也，而何怪！

translations.literal: Bian Que entered to examine the illness and came out. Dong Anyu asked Bian Que, and Bian Que said: "The blood vessels are in order—what is there to marvel at?"
translations.idiomatic: Bian Que went in to examine the illness, then came out. Dong Anyu questioned him, and Bian Que said: "His blood vessels are functioning properly—why all the alarm?"

sentences.zh: 昔秦穆公嘗如此，七日而寤。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Mu of Qin was once like this, after seven days he awoke.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, Duke Mu of Qin once suffered the same condition, and after seven days he awoke.

sentences.zh: 寤之日，告公孫支與子輿曰：『我之帝所甚樂。

translations.literal: On the day he awoke, he told Gongsun Zhi and Ziyu: "I was greatly pleased at the Emperor's court.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he regained consciousness, he told Gongsun Zhi and Ziyu: "I found great delight in the place of the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 吾所以久者，適有所學也。

translations.literal: The reason I stayed so long was that I had something to learn.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I was gone so long was that I had something yet to learn there.

sentences.zh: 帝告我：「晉國且大亂，五世不安。

translations.literal: The Emperor told me: "The state of Jin will soon fall into great disorder; five generations will know no peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to me: "The state of Jin is about to suffer great chaos, and five generations will not know tranquility.

sentences.zh: 其後將霸，未老而死。

translations.literal: Afterward it will become hegemon, but die before old age.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, your heir will rise to hegemony but will die before reaching old age.

sentences.zh: 霸者之子且令而國男女無別。」』

translations.literal: The son of the hegemon will cause men and women in his state to be undifferentiated."'
translations.idiomatic: The heir who becomes hegemon will bring it about that in his state there will be no distinction between men and women."'

sentences.zh: 公孫支書而藏之，秦策於是出。

translations.literal: Gongsun Zhi wrote it and hid it, and the Qin strategies emerged from this.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Zhi wrote it all down and stored the record away, and from this the Stratagems of Qin came into being.

sentences.zh: 夫獻公之亂，文公之霸，而襄公敗秦師於殽而歸縱淫，此子之所聞。

translations.literal: Duke Xian's chaos, Duke Wen's hegemony, Duke Xiang defeating the Qin army at Xiao and returning to indulge in lewdness—this is what the son has heard.
translations.idiomatic: The disorders under Duke Xian, the hegemony under Duke Wen, and Duke Xiang's defeat of the Qin army at Xiao followed by his return to indulge in excess—all of this is what you have already heard.

sentences.zh: 今主君之病與之同，不出三日必閒，閒必有言也。」

translations.literal: Now my lord's illness is the same; within three days he is sure to recover consciousness, and when he does he will certainly have something to say."
translations.idiomatic: Now the lord's illness matches that case; before three days are out he is certain to awaken, and when he awakens he will surely have words to speak."

sentences.zh: 居二日半，簡子寤，語諸大夫曰：「我之帝所甚樂，與百神游於鈞天，廣樂九奏萬舞，不類三代之樂，其聲動心。

translations.literal: After two and a half days, Jianzi awoke and said to the various ministers: "I was greatly pleased at the Emperor's court, wandering with the hundred spirits in the Grand Heaven; broad music with nine performances and myriad dances—not like the music of the Three Dynasties, yet its sound moved the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Two and a half days later Jianzi regained consciousness and addressed the ministers: "I was filled with joy in the Emperor's dwelling, roaming with the hundred spirits in the Harmonious Heaven. Grand music sounded in nine suites and ten thousand dancers performed—unlike the music of the Three Dynasties, yet its sound stirred my heart.

sentences.zh: 有一熊欲援我，帝命我射之，中熊，熊死。

translations.literal: There was a bear that wanted to attack me, the emperor commanded me to shoot it, I hit the bear, the bear died.
translations.idiomatic: A bear lunged at me, and the Emperor commanded me to shoot it. My arrow struck the bear, and it fell dead.

sentences.zh: 有羆來，我又射之，中羆，羆死。

translations.literal: A great bear came; I shot it again, hit the bear, and the bear died.
translations.idiomatic: Then a brown bear appeared, and I shot it as well. My arrow struck home, and it too fell dead.

sentences.zh: 帝甚喜，賜我二笥，皆有副。

translations.literal: The emperor was very pleased, granted me two baskets, both with duplicates.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed upon me two baskets, each with a matching pair.

sentences.zh: 吾見兒在帝側，帝屬我一翟犬，曰：『及而子之壯也以賜之。』

translations.literal: I saw a child at the Emperor's side; the Emperor entrusted me with a Di hound, saying: "When your son grows strong, give it to him."
translations.idiomatic: I saw a boy at the Emperor's side. The Emperor placed a Di dog in my charge, saying: "When your son reaches his prime, bestow it upon him."

sentences.zh: 帝告我：『晉國且世衰，七世而亡。

translations.literal: The Emperor told me: "The state of Jin will decline generation by generation; after seven generations it will perish.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to me: "Jin will wane from age to age, and after seven generations it will be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 嬴姓將大敗周人於范魁之西，而亦不能有也。』」

translations.literal: The Ying clan will inflict a great defeat on the Zhou people west of Fan Kui, yet will not be able to hold the territory."'"
translations.idiomatic: The house of Ying will deal the Zhou people a great defeat west of Fan and Kui, but will not be able to keep what they win."'"

sentences.zh: 董安于受言，書而藏之。

translations.literal: Dong Anyu received the account, wrote it down, and stored it away.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Anyu took in what had been said, committed it to writing, and put the record in safekeeping.

sentences.zh: 以扁鵲言告簡子，簡子賜扁鵲田四萬畝。

translations.literal: He reported Bian Que's words to Jianzi, and Jianzi granted Bian Que forty thousand mu of fields.
translations.idiomatic: He relayed Bian Que's prophecy to Jianzi, and Jianzi rewarded Bian Que with forty thousand mu of land.

sentences.zh: 其後扁鵲過虢。

translations.literal: Later, Bian Que passed through the state of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Some time afterward, Bian Que traveled through Guo.

sentences.zh: 虢太子死，扁鵲至虢宮門下，問中庶子喜方者曰：「太子何病，國中治穰過於眾事？」

translations.literal: The crown prince of Guo had died. Bian Que came to the gate of the Guo palace and asked the palace attendant Xifang, who was fond of medicine: "What illness did the crown prince have, that the state's mourning rites should exceed all other affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent of Guo had died. When Bian Que reached the palace gate of Guo, he questioned the palace attendant Xifang, who delighted in medical formulas: "What malady afflicted the crown prince, that the kingdom should mourn him with ceremonies more elaborate than for any other matter?"

sentences.zh: 中庶子曰：「太子病血氣不時，交錯而不得泄，暴發於外，則為中害。

translations.literal: The palace attendant said: "The crown prince's illness was that his blood and qi were irregular, entangled and unable to be released; when it suddenly erupted outward, it became internal harm.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant replied: "The crown prince suffered from irregular blood and qi that became entangled and could not discharge. When it burst outward, it caused internal damage.

sentences.zh: 精神不能止邪氣，邪氣畜積而不得泄，是以陽緩而陰急，故暴蹷而死。」

translations.literal: His spirit could not restrain the evil qi; the evil qi accumulated and could not be released. Thus yang was sluggish and yin urgent, and so he suddenly collapsed and died."
translations.idiomatic: His vital spirit could not check the pathogenic influences, which built up and remained trapped. Yang grew slack while yin turned urgent, and he died in a sudden collapse."

sentences.zh: 扁鵲曰：「其死何如時？」

translations.literal: Bian Que said: "At what time did he die?"
translations.idiomatic: Bian Que asked: "When did he die?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「雞鳴至今。」

translations.literal: He said: "From cockcrow until now."
translations.idiomatic: The attendant answered: "From cockcrow until now."

sentences.zh: 曰：「收乎？」

translations.literal: Bian Que asked: "Has he been encoffined?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked: "Has the body been prepared for burial?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「未也，其死未能半日也。」

translations.literal: He said: "Not yet; he has been dead less than half a day."
translations.idiomatic: The attendant replied: "Not yet—he has been dead less than half a day."

sentences.zh: 「言臣齊勃海秦越人也，家在於鄭，未嘗得望精光侍謁於前也。

translations.literal: "I am Yueren of Qi, from Bohai, of the Qin clan; my home is in Zheng. I have never yet had the honor of beholding your radiance and attending before you.
translations.idiomatic: "Your servant is Qin Yueren of Bohai in Qi, with my household at Zheng. I have never been privileged to gaze upon your splendor and serve in your presence.

sentences.zh: 聞太子不幸而死，臣能生之。」

translations.literal: I have heard that the crown prince has met with misfortune and died; your servant can revive him."
translations.idiomatic: I have learned that the crown prince has unfortunately died. I can bring him back to life."

sentences.zh: 中庶子曰：「先生得無誕之乎？

translations.literal: The palace attendant said: "Surely you are not jesting, Master?
translations.idiomatic: The palace attendant said: "Sir, you cannot be speaking in jest?

sentences.zh: 何以言太子可生也！

translations.literal: How can you say the crown prince can be revived!
translations.idiomatic: How can you claim the crown prince may be brought back to life!

sentences.zh: 臣聞上古之時，醫有俞跗，治病不以湯液醴灑，鑱石撟引，案扤毒熨，一撥見病之應，因五藏之輸，乃割皮解肌，訣脈結筋，搦髓腦，揲荒爪幕，湔浣腸胃，漱滌五藏，練精易形。

translations.literal: I have heard that in high antiquity there was a physician named Yu Fu. He treated illness without decoctions or medicinal washes, but used stone needles, traction, pressing and poisonous hot compresses; with one touch he saw the illness's response. Following the conduits of the five viscera, he would cut the skin and separate the flesh, untie the vessels and bind the sinews, probe the marrow and brain, lift the membranes, wash the intestines and stomach, rinse the five viscera, refine the essence and change the form.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that in remote antiquity the physician Yu Fu practiced without broths or rinses, but with stone needles, manipulation, pressing, and heated compresses charged with toxins. A single probing revealed how the disease responded. He followed the pathways of the five organs—cutting skin, parting flesh, releasing vessels and tying sinews, reaching marrow and brain, lifting membranes, cleansing bowels and stomach, washing the five organs, refining essence, even transforming the body itself.

sentences.zh: 先生之方能若是，則太子可生也；

translations.literal: If your art were like his, then the crown prince could live;
translations.idiomatic: If your skill truly matched his, the crown prince might indeed be saved;

sentences.zh: 不能若是而欲生之，曾不可以告咳嬰之兒。」

translations.literal: but if it is not like that and you still wish to revive him, you could not even convince a coughing infant."
translations.idiomatic: yet if your methods fall short of that and you still claim you can revive him, you might as well tell it to a child who is coughing."

sentences.zh: 終日，扁鵲仰天嘆曰：「夫子之為方也，若以管窺天，以郄視文。

translations.literal: All that day Bian Que looked up to heaven and sighed: "Sir, in practicing medicine you are like viewing heaven through a tube or reading a pattern through a narrow crack.
translations.idiomatic: When the day was done, Bian Que gazed skyward and sighed: "Master, in your practice of medicine you are like peering at the sky through a bamboo tube or studying brocade through a chink in the wall.

sentences.zh: 越人之為方也，不待切脈望色聽聲寫形，言病之所在。

translations.literal: Yue Ren's method did not wait for pulse cutting, complexion observation, sound listening, or form recording to speak of the illness's location.
translations.idiomatic: Yueren's method of medicine did not require feeling the pulse, observing the complexion, listening to the voice, or examining the body to identify the location of a disease.

sentences.zh: 聞病之陽，論得其陰；

translations.literal: Hearing the yang of an illness, he discussed and obtained its yin;
translations.idiomatic: From the outward signs of a disease he could reason out its hidden aspect;

sentences.zh: 聞病之陰，論得其陽。

translations.literal: Hearing the illness's yin, he discussed and obtained its yang.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard the hidden aspects of a disease, he could deduce its outward manifestations.

sentences.zh: 病應見於大表，不出千里，決者至眾，不可曲止也。

translations.literal: The illness should appear on the great surface, not going beyond a thousand li, those who decide reach many, cannot be arbitrarily stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The signs of a disease manifest on the body's surface, and his diagnoses proved accurate across a thousand li. The cases he resolved were innumerable, and his reputation could not be contained.

sentences.zh: 子以吾言為不誠，試入診太子，當聞其耳鳴而鼻張，循其兩股以至於陰，當尚溫也。」

translations.literal: If you consider my words insincere, try entering to examine the crown prince: you should hear his ears ringing and his nostrils flaring; follow along both thighs down to the genital region—it should still be warm."
translations.idiomatic: If you doubt my sincerity, go in and examine the crown prince yourself. You will hear ringing in his ears and see his nostrils distended; if you trace both thighs down to the yin region, you should find it still warm."

sentences.zh: 中庶子聞扁鵲言，目眩然而不瞚，舌撟然而不下，乃以扁鵲言入報虢君。

translations.literal: The palace attendant heard Bian Que's words, eyes dazzled but not blinking, tongue extended but not descending, then entered with Bian Que's words to report to the Guo ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace attendant heard Bian Que's words, his eyes went wide and did not blink, his tongue hung slack and would not retract. He then went inside to relay Bian Que's message to the Lord of Guo.

sentences.zh: 虢君聞之大驚，出見扁鵲於中闕，曰：「竊聞高義之日久矣，然未嘗得拜謁於前也。

translations.literal: The Lord of Guo heard and was greatly alarmed. He came out to meet Bian Que at the central gate and said: "I have long heard in secret of your lofty righteousness, yet never once had the honor of bowing before you.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lord of Guo heard this, he was deeply shaken. He went out to receive Bian Que at the middle gate and said: "I have privately admired your noble conduct for many years, yet never until now had the chance to pay my respects in person.

sentences.zh: 先生過小國，幸而舉之，偏國寡臣幸甚。

translations.literal: Sir passes through our small state, fortunately raises this matter, our partial state and few ministers are very fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: That you, sir, should pass through our small state and deign to take up this matter—our remote kingdom and its humble ministers are most fortunate indeed.

sentences.zh: 有先生則活，無先生則棄捐填溝壑，長終而不得反。」

translations.literal: With you, sir, he lives; without you, sir, he is abandoned to fill ravines and gullies, ended forever with no return."
translations.idiomatic: If you, sir, are here, he may live; if you are not, he will be cast away to choke the ditches and valleys, lost forever without hope of return."

sentences.zh: 言末卒，因噓唏服臆，魂精泄橫，流涕長潸，忽忽承睫，悲不能自止，容貌變更。

translations.literal: The words not yet finished, he sighed and wept embracing his breast, soul essence leaking horizontally, flowing tears long moistening, suddenly accepting the eyelashes, sorrow could not be stopped by himself, appearance changed.
translations.idiomatic: Before the lord could finish speaking, he broke into heaving sobs, clutching his breast. His spirit seemed to drain from him, tears streamed unceasingly down his cheeks, brimming along his lashes, and his grief became so overwhelming that he could not restrain it. His very countenance was transformed.

sentences.zh: 扁鵲曰：「若太子病，所謂『尸蹷』者也。

translations.literal: Bian Que said: "The crown prince's illness is what is called 'corpse syncope.'"
translations.idiomatic: Bian Que said: "The crown prince's condition is what is termed 'corpse syncope.'"

sentences.zh: 夫以陽入陰中，動胃繵緣，中經維絡，別下於三焦、膀胱，是以陽脈下遂，陰脈上爭，會氣閉而不通，陰上而陽內行，下內鼓而不起，上外絕而不為使，上有絕陽之絡，下有破陰之紐，破陰絕陽，（之）色［已］廢脈亂，故形靜如死狀。

translations.literal: Because yang entered the yin center, moved the stomach and entangled the vessels, through the central classics and binding networks, separately descending to the three burners and bladder, therefore yang pulses descended and followed, yin pulses ascended and contended, meeting energies closed and not through, yin ascended yet yang walked inwardly, lower internal drumming yet not rising, upper external severance yet not functioning, above having severed yang networks, below having broken yin knots, broken yin severed yang, appearance already wasted pulses chaotic, therefore form quiet like death shape.
translations.idiomatic: What happened is that yang energy entered the yin regions, agitating the stomach and entangling the vessels. It passed through the central channels and connecting networks, then descended separately to the triple burner and the bladder. As a result, the yang pulses sank downward while the yin pulses surged upward in contention. Where the vital energies converged, they became blocked and could not circulate—yin rose while yang turned inward. Below, the inner organs churned without the strength to rise; above, the outer connections were severed and could not function. Above there were severed yang channels, below there were ruptured yin junctures. With yin broken and yang cut off, the complexion faded and the pulse fell into disorder. Thus the body lay still as though dead.

sentences.zh: 太子未死也。

translations.literal: The crown prince is not dead.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is not dead.

sentences.zh: 夫以陽入陰支蘭藏者生，以陰入陽支蘭藏者死。

translations.literal: Because yang entering yin branch vessels lives, yin entering yang branch vessels dies.
translations.idiomatic: When yang energy enters the yin branch vessels and reaches the organs, the patient lives; when yin energy enters the yang branch vessels and reaches the organs, the patient dies.

sentences.zh: 凡此數事，皆五藏蹙中之時暴作也。

translations.literal: All these several matters are all sudden attacks at the time of the five viscera's contraction.
translations.idiomatic: All such cases arise from sudden seizures that occur when the five organs are thrown into spasm.

sentences.zh: 良工取之，拙者疑殆。」

translations.literal: A skilled craftsman takes the case; a clumsy one doubts and hesitates."
translations.idiomatic: A master physician accepts it; a bungler only doubts and stalls."

sentences.zh: 扁鵲乃使弟子子陽厲鍼砥石，以取外三陽五會。

translations.literal: Bian Que then had his disciple Ziyang sharpen the needle on stone, to take the outer three yang and five convergence points.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Que then had his disciple Ziyang hone a needle against a whetstone and apply it to the outer Three Yang and Five Convergence acupuncture points.

sentences.zh: 有閒，太子蘇。

translations.literal: After an interval, the crown prince revived.
translations.idiomatic: After a short while, the crown prince revived.

sentences.zh: 乃使子豹為五分之熨，以八減之齊和煮之，以更熨兩脅下。

translations.literal: Then he had Zibao make a five-part compress, mixed and boiled with an eight-reduction decoction, to alternately compress both sides below.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Zibao prepare a five-part compress, blending and boiling it with an eight-reduction decoction, and applied the hot compresses alternately beneath both flanks.

sentences.zh: 太子起坐。

translations.literal: The crown prince sat up.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince sat up.

sentences.zh: 更適陰陽，但服湯二旬而復故。

translations.literal: He adjusted yin and yang more, but after taking the decoction for twenty days he recovered as before.
translations.idiomatic: He further regulated the balance of yin and yang, and after the prince took the medicinal broth for twenty days, he made a full recovery.

sentences.zh: 故天下盡以扁鵲為能生死人。

translations.literal: Therefore all under heaven considered Bian Que able to bring the dead back to life.
translations.idiomatic: And so all the world came to believe that Bian Que could raise the dead.

sentences.zh: 扁鵲曰：「越人非能生死人也，此自當生者，越人能使之起耳。」

translations.literal: Bian Que said: "Yueren cannot bring the dead back to life. These are people who were fated to live; Yueren can only rouse them."
translations.idiomatic: Bian Que said: "I, Yueren, do not restore the dead to life. Such persons were already destined to survive—I merely help them rise."

sentences.zh: 扁鵲過齊，齊桓侯客之。

translations.literal: Bian Que passed through Qi, Duke Huan of Qi hosted him.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Que once passed through the state of Qi, and Marquis Huan of Qi received him as a guest.

sentences.zh: 入朝見，曰：「君有疾在腠理，不治將深。」

translations.literal: Entering the court to pay his respects, he said: "Your lordship has an illness in the interstices of the flesh; if it is not treated, it will go deep."
translations.idiomatic: When he entered court and was received, he said: "Your lordship has a malady in the skin and flesh; unless it is treated, it will penetrate deeper."

sentences.zh: 桓侯曰：「寡人無疾。」

translations.literal: Duke Huan said: "I have no illness."
translations.idiomatic: The marquis replied: "I am not ill."

sentences.zh: 扁鵲出，桓侯謂左右曰：「醫之好利也，欲以不疾者為功。」

translations.literal: Bian Que withdrew, and Duke Huan said to those beside him: "Physicians love profit; they wish to claim merit by treating those who are not ill."
translations.idiomatic: Bian Que left, and the marquis told his attendants: "Doctors are greedy for gain—they want credit for curing people who are not sick."

sentences.zh: 後五日，扁鵲復見，曰：「君有疾在血脈，不治恐深。」

translations.literal: Five days later Bian Que saw him again and said: "Your lordship has an illness in the blood vessels; if it is not treated, I fear it will go deep."
translations.idiomatic: Five days later Bian Que visited him again and said: "Your lordship has a malady in the blood vessels; unless it is treated, I fear it will worsen."

sentences.zh: 桓侯曰：「寡人無疾。」

translations.literal: Duke Huan said: "I have no illness."
translations.idiomatic: The marquis again said: "I am not ill."

sentences.zh: 扁鵲出，桓侯不悅。

translations.literal: Bian Que left, Duke Huan was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: After Bian Que withdrew, the marquis was displeased.

sentences.zh: 後五日，扁鵲復見，曰；

translations.literal: After five days, Bian Que again see, said;
translations.idiomatic: After five days, Bian Que saw him again, saying:

sentences.zh: 「君有疾在腸胃閒，不治將深。」

translations.literal: "Your lordship has an illness between the intestines and stomach; if it is not treated, it will go deep."
translations.idiomatic: "Your lordship has a malady in the intestines and stomach; unless it is treated, it will penetrate further."

sentences.zh: 桓侯不應。

translations.literal: Duke Huan did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: The marquis made no reply.

sentences.zh: 扁鵲出，桓侯不悅。

translations.literal: Bian Que left, Duke Huan was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Once again Bian Que withdrew, and the marquis was displeased.

sentences.zh: 後五日，扁鵲復見，望見桓侯而退走。

translations.literal: After five days, Bian Que saw him again, but seeing Duke Huan he retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later, Bian Que came to see the marquis again, but the moment he caught sight of him, he turned and hurried away.

sentences.zh: 桓侯使人問其故。

translations.literal: Duke Huan sent someone to ask the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The marquis sent someone to ask him why.

sentences.zh: 扁鵲曰：「疾之居腠理也，湯熨之所及也；

translations.literal: Bian Que said: "When an illness dwells in the interstices of the flesh, hot compresses and decoctions can reach it;
translations.idiomatic: Bian Que said: "When the disease sits in the skin and flesh, broths and hot compresses can still reach it;

sentences.zh: 在血脈，鍼石之所及也；

translations.literal: in the blood vessels, needles and stones can reach it;
translations.idiomatic: when it is in the blood vessels, acupuncture and stone needles can reach it;

sentences.zh: 其在腸胃，酒醪之所及也；

translations.literal: when it is in the intestines and stomach, medicinal wine can reach it;
translations.idiomatic: when it lies in the intestines and stomach, wine-based medicines can still reach it;

sentences.zh: 其在骨髓，雖司命無柰之何。

translations.literal: When it is in the bone marrow, even the Controller of Fate can do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: Once the disease has reached the bone marrow, even the god who governs fate can do nothing about it.

sentences.zh: 今在骨髓，臣是以無請也。」

translations.literal: Now it is in the bone marrow, so your servant has no request to make."
translations.idiomatic: Now it has entered the bone marrow, and therefore I have nothing further to ask."

sentences.zh: 後五日，桓侯體病，使人召扁鵲，扁鵲已逃去。

translations.literal: After five days, Duke Huan's body became ill, he sent someone to summon Bian Que, but Bian Que had already fled.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later, the marquis fell ill. He sent someone to summon Bian Que, but the physician had already fled.

sentences.zh: 桓侯遂死。

translations.literal: Duke Huan then died.
translations.idiomatic: The marquis died soon after.

sentences.zh: 使聖人預知微，能使良醫得蚤從事，則疾可已，身可活也。

translations.literal: If sages could foreknow the subtle, able to make good physicians begin affairs early, then illnesses could be cured, bodies could live.
translations.idiomatic: If only the wise could perceive the subtle signs early and allow a skilled physician to intervene in time, then the disease could be cured and the patient's life could be saved.

sentences.zh: 人之所病，病疾多；

translations.literal: What people suffer from is that illnesses are many;
translations.idiomatic: What people are afflicted with is that diseases are numerous;

sentences.zh: 而醫之所病，病道少。

translations.literal: But what physicians suffer from illness, illnesses of the Way are few.
translations.idiomatic: What physicians truly suffer from is that there are too few paths to healing.

sentences.zh: 故病有六不治：驕恣不論於理，一不治也；

translations.literal: Therefore illness have six not treat: arrogant zi not discuss at li, one not treat;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore illnesses have six that are not treated: arrogant indulgence not discussed according to principle, first not treated;

sentences.zh: 輕身重財，二不治也；

translations.literal: valuing wealth more than life, second not treated;
translations.idiomatic: treating wealth as light and life as heavy—the second case not treated;

sentences.zh: 衣食不能適，三不治也；

translations.literal: Clothes food cannot adapt, three not treat;
translations.idiomatic: Clothing and food cannot be adapted, third not treated;

sentences.zh: 陰陽并，藏氣不定，四不治也；

translations.literal: Yin yang bing, hide qi not fixed, four not treat;
translations.idiomatic: Yin and yang confused, visceral energies not settled, fourth not treated;

sentences.zh: 形羸不能服藥，五不治也；

translations.literal: Shape lean cannot serve medicine, five not treat;
translations.idiomatic: Body emaciated cannot take medicine, fifth not treated;

sentences.zh: 信巫不信醫，六不治也。

translations.literal: Believing shamans not believing physicians, sixth not treated.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth is when the patient trusts shamans rather than physicians—such a person cannot be treated.

sentences.zh: 有此一者，則重難治也。

translations.literal: Having one of these, then it is very difficult to treat.
translations.idiomatic: If even one of these conditions applies, the case becomes exceedingly difficult to treat.

sentences.zh: 扁鵲名聞天下。

translations.literal: Bian Que's name was heard throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Que's fame spread throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 過邯鄲，聞貴婦人，即為帶下醫；

translations.literal: Passing through Handan, hearing that people there valued women, he became a physician for gynecological disorders;
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Handan, where he heard that women were held in esteem, he practiced as a physician for women's ailments;

sentences.zh: 過雒陽，聞周人愛老人，即為耳目痹醫；

translations.literal: Pass Luo Yang, hear Zhou person love old person, then become ear eye bi doctor;
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Luoyang, hearing that Zhou people loved the elderly, he then became a physician for ear and eye ailments;

sentences.zh: 來入咸陽，聞秦人愛小兒，即為小兒醫：隨俗為變。

translations.literal: Coming to Xianyang, hearing that the people of Qin loved children, he became a children's physician: he changed according to local custom.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered Xianyang and learned that the Qin people cherished their young, he became a pediatrician—adapting his practice to each region's customs.

sentences.zh: 秦太醫令李醯自知伎不如扁鵲也，使人刺殺之。

translations.literal: The Qin Chief Physician Li Xi himself knew his skills were not equal to Bian Que's, so he sent someone to assassinate him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi, the Chief Physician of Qin, knew in his heart that his own skills could not match those of Bian Que. He sent someone to assassinate him.

sentences.zh: 至今天下言脈者，由扁鵲也。

translations.literal: Until today when all under heaven speak of pulse diagnosis, it originates from Bian Que.
translations.idiomatic: To this day, whenever anyone in the realm speaks of pulse diagnosis, it traces back to Bian Que.

sentences.zh: 太倉公者，齊太倉長，臨菑人也，姓淳于氏，名意。

translations.literal: Tai Cang Gong was the Qi granary director, a Linzi person, surname Chunyu, given name Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Granary Master was the director of the state granary of Qi. He was a native of Linzi, with the surname Chunyu and the given name Yi.

sentences.zh: 少而喜醫方術。

translations.literal: In youth he delighted in medical arts and techniques.
translations.idiomatic: From a young age, he took delight in the art and techniques of medicine.

sentences.zh: 高后八年，更受師同郡元里公乘陽慶。

translations.literal: In Empress Gao's eighth year, he again received teachings from his fellow commandery man, Gongcheng Yang Qing of Yuanli.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Empress Gao's reign, he took on a new teacher: Yang Qing, a man of the Gongcheng rank from Yuanli in the same commandery.

sentences.zh: 慶年七十餘，無子，使意盡去其故方，更悉以禁方予之，傳黃帝、扁鵲之脈書，五色診病，知人死生，決嫌疑，定可治，及藥論，甚精。

translations.literal: Qing was over seventy years old, had no son, made Yi completely abandon his old prescriptions, and moreover gave him all the secret prescriptions, transmitting the Yellow Emperor and Bian Que's pulse books, five-color diagnosis of illness, knowing people's death and life, deciding suspicions, fixing what can be treated, and medicine discussions, very refined.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was over seventy years old and had no sons. He made Yi discard all of his old prescriptions and in their place gave him every one of his secret formulas. He transmitted to Yi the pulse texts of the Yellow Emperor and Bian Que, the method of diagnosing illness through the five colors, the art of determining life and death, the resolution of ambiguous cases, the identification of treatable conditions, and the theory of pharmacology—all of it extraordinarily refined.

sentences.zh: 受之三年，為人治病，決死生多驗。

translations.literal: After receiving teachings for three years, when treating people's illnesses, his decisions on death and life were mostly verified.
translations.idiomatic: After three years of study, when he treated patients, his predictions of life and death proved correct more often than not.

sentences.zh: 然左右行游諸侯，不以家為家，或不為人治病，病家多怨之者。

translations.literal: Yet he traveled left and right among the various feudal lords, not considering home as home, sometimes not treating people's illnesses, the ill families mostly resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he wandered here and there among the feudal lords, never settling down at home, and at times refused to treat patients. Many families with sick members came to resent him for this.

sentences.zh: 文帝四年中，人上書言意，以刑罪當傳西之長安。

translations.literal: In the middle of Emperor Wen's fourth year, someone submitted a memorial speaking of Yi, who due to criminal punishment should be transported west to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Emperor Wen's reign, someone submitted a memorial denouncing Yi, and as a result he was sentenced to corporal punishment and was to be transported west to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 意有五女，隨而泣。

translations.literal: Yi had five daughters, who followed him weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had five daughters, and they followed after him, weeping.

sentences.zh: 意怒，罵曰：「生子不生男，緩急無可使者！」

translations.literal: Yi was angry and cursed, saying: "Bearing children but not bearing sons—in urgency there is no one to send!"
translations.idiomatic: Yi grew angry and scolded them: "To bear children yet not bear sons—when trouble comes there is no one to dispatch!"

sentences.zh: 於是少女緹縈傷父之言，乃隨父西。

translations.literal: Then the youngest daughter Tiying was hurt by her father's words, and followed her father west.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest daughter, Tiying, was pained by her father's words and followed him west.

sentences.zh: 上書曰：「妾父為吏，齊中稱其廉平，今坐法當刑。

translations.literal: She submitted a memorial saying: "My father serves as an official; in Qi he is called upright and fair. Now he has been convicted by law and should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: She submitted a memorial that read: "My father has served as an official and is praised in Qi for his integrity and fairness. Now he has been found guilty under the law and is to be punished.

sentences.zh: 妾切痛死者不可復生而刑者不可復續，雖欲改過自新，其道莫由，終不可得。

translations.literal: I deeply grieve that the dead cannot be brought back to life and the punished cannot have their bodies restored, though desiring to reform faults and renew themselves, there is no way, ultimately cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: I am deeply grieved that the dead cannot be brought back to life and that those who have suffered mutilation can never be made whole again. Though they may wish to reform their ways and start anew, there is no path left to them, and such a chance can never be obtained.

sentences.zh: 妾願入身為官婢，以贖父刑罪，使得改行自新也。」

translations.literal: I wish to enter my person as an official slave to redeem my father's punishment, so that he may reform his conduct and renew himself."
translations.idiomatic: I beg to offer myself as a palace bondwoman to redeem my father's sentence, that he may be given the chance to change his ways and begin anew."

sentences.zh: 書聞，上悲其意，此歲中亦除肉刑法。

translations.literal: The memorial was heard, the emperor was saddened by her intent, and in the middle of this year also abolished the mutilating punishment laws.
translations.idiomatic: When her memorial reached the throne, the emperor was moved by her devotion. In the course of that same year, he abolished the laws prescribing mutilating punishments.

sentences.zh: 意家居，詔召問所為治病死生驗者幾何人也，主名為誰。

translations.literal: Yi resided at home, an edict summoned him and asked how many people he had treated for illnesses with verified predictions of death and life, and whose main names they were.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi was living at home, an imperial edict summoned him and asked how many patients he had treated whose outcomes of life and death he had accurately predicted, and what their names were.

sentences.zh: 詔問故太倉長臣意：「方伎所長，及所能治病者？

translations.literal: The edict asked the former granary director, Minister Yi: "What medical arts are you skilled in, and what illnesses can you treat?"
translations.idiomatic: The edict inquired of the former granary director, Minister Yi: "In what therapeutic arts do you excel, and what sorts of illness can you treat?"

sentences.zh: 有其書無有？

translations.literal: Do you have the books or not?
translations.idiomatic: Do you possess the relevant texts or not?

sentences.zh: 皆安受學？

translations.literal: Where did you all receive your instruction?
translations.idiomatic: From whom did you receive your training?

sentences.zh: 受學幾何歲？

translations.literal: For how many years did you study?
translations.idiomatic: How many years did you study under them?

sentences.zh: 嘗有所驗，何縣里人也？

translations.literal: What cases have you verified, and what district and hamlet were the patients from?
translations.idiomatic: What outcomes have you verified, and in which counties and villages did those patients live?

sentences.zh: 何病？

translations.literal: What illness?
translations.idiomatic: What was the illness?

sentences.zh: 醫藥已，其病之狀皆何如？

translations.literal: Doctor medicine already, its illness shape all what like?
translations.idiomatic: After doctor and medicine, what was the condition of the illness like?

sentences.zh: 具悉而對。」

translations.literal: Report everything in full."'
translations.idiomatic: Give a complete and detailed reply."'

sentences.zh: 臣意對曰：

translations.literal: I replied:
translations.idiomatic: I answered:

sentences.zh: 自意少時，喜醫藥，醫藥方試之多不驗者。

translations.literal: From Yi's youth, he delighted in medicine, but tried many medical methods that were not verified.
translations.idiomatic: From the time I was young, I took delight in medicine, but the many remedies I tried in those days rarely proved effective.

sentences.zh: 至高后八年，得見師臨菑元里公乘陽慶。

translations.literal: Until Empress Gao's eighth year, he obtained to see the teacher Gongcheng Yang Qing of Linzi Yuanli.
translations.idiomatic: It was not until the eighth year of Empress Gao's reign that I was able to study under the master Yang Qing, a man of the Gongcheng rank from Yuanli in Linzi.

sentences.zh: 慶年七十餘，意得見事之。

translations.literal: Qing was over seventy years old, Yi obtained to see and serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was over seventy years old, and I was permitted to attend and serve him.

sentences.zh: 謂意曰：「盡去而方書，非是也。

translations.literal: Speak Yi said: "All go your recipe book, not this.
translations.idiomatic: He said to Yi: "Completely abandon your prescription books, they are not this.

sentences.zh: 慶有古先道遺傳黃帝、扁鵲之脈書，五色診病，知人生死，決嫌疑，定可治，及藥論書，甚精。

translations.literal: Qing has ancient transmitted teachings of the Yellow Emperor and Bian Que's pulse books, five-color diagnosis of illness, knowing people's life and death, deciding suspicions, fixing what can be treated, and medicine discussion books, very refined.
translations.idiomatic: Qing possessed the ancient teachings transmitted from antiquity: the pulse texts of the Yellow Emperor and Bian Que, the method of diagnosing illness through the five colors, the art of determining life and death, the resolution of ambiguous cases, the identification of treatable conditions, and treatises on pharmacology—all extraordinarily refined.

sentences.zh: 我家給富，心愛公，欲盡以我禁方書悉教公。」

translations.literal: My household is wealthy; I hold you in affection and wish to teach you every one of my secret prescription books."
translations.idiomatic: My family is well provided for. I esteem you and desire to transmit to you in full all my books of secret formulas."

sentences.zh: 臣意即曰：「幸甚，非意之所敢望也。」

translations.literal: I immediately said: "This is most fortunate—more than I dared hope for."
translations.idiomatic: I answered at once: "I am deeply fortunate; it is beyond what I had dared to expect."

sentences.zh: 臣意即避席再拜謁，受其脈書上下經、五色診、奇咳術、揆度陰陽外變、藥論、石神、接陰陽禁書，受讀解驗之，可一年所。

translations.literal: Minister Yi then left his seat and bowed twice in respect, received his pulse books of upper and lower classics, five-color diagnosis, strange cough techniques, measuring yin and yang external changes, medicine discussions, stone gods, connecting yin and yang forbidden books, received them and read, explained, and verified them, taking about a year.
translations.idiomatic: I then rose from my seat, prostrated myself twice in gratitude, and received from him the pulse texts of the Upper and Lower Classics, the Five-Color Diagnosis, the Art of Treating Unusual Coughs, the Measurement of External Changes in Yin and Yang, the Treatise on Pharmacology, the Divine Properties of Mineral Remedies, and the Forbidden Texts on the Union of Yin and Yang. I received, read, interpreted, and tested them over the course of approximately one year.

sentences.zh: 明歲即驗之，有驗，然尚未精也。

translations.literal: The next year he then verified them, there were verifications, but not yet refined.
translations.idiomatic: The following year I put them to the test, and the results proved valid, though my skills were still far from refined.

sentences.zh: 要事之三年所，即嘗已為人治，診病決死生，有驗，精良。

translations.literal: After three years of important study, then he once treated people, diagnosing illnesses and deciding death and life, there were verifications, refined and good.
translations.idiomatic: After roughly three years of intensive study, I began treating patients in earnest, diagnosing their illnesses and predicting life or death. My results were verified and had grown refined and reliable.

sentences.zh: 今慶已死十年所，臣意年盡三年，年三十九歲也。

translations.literal: Now Qing has been dead for about ten years, Minister Yi has completed three years of age, is thirty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: It has now been about ten years since Qing's death. I have been studying for a full three years and am thirty-nine years of age.

sentences.zh: 齊侍御史成自言病頭痛，臣意診其脈，告曰：「君之病惡，不可言也。」

translations.literal: Cheng, an attendant censor of Qi, said himself that he suffered headaches. I felt his pulse and reported: "Your illness is grave and cannot be put into words."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng, a palace censor in Qi, complained of headaches. When I examined his pulse I told him: "Your disease is severe—so severe it cannot be spoken of."

sentences.zh: 即出，獨告成弟昌曰：「此病疽也，內發於腸胃之閒，後五日當擁腫，後八日嘔膿死。」

translations.literal: Then exit, alone tell Cheng brother Chang said: "This illness ju, inner send at intestine stomach interval, after five days should yong zhong, after eight days ou nong die."
translations.idiomatic: Then he left, alone told Cheng's brother Chang: "This illness is a carbuncle, internally developing in the space between intestines and stomach, after five days it should swell and gather, after eight days vomit pus and die."

sentences.zh: 成之病得之飲酒且內。

translations.literal: Cheng's illness came from drinking wine and sexual excess.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's illness arose from excessive drinking and sexual indulgence.

sentences.zh: 成即如期死。

translations.literal: Cheng then died as predicted.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng died precisely when predicted.

sentences.zh: 所以知成之病者，臣意切其脈，得肝氣。

translations.literal: The reason I knew Cheng's illness was that Minister Yi cut his pulse and obtained liver energy.
translations.idiomatic: The way I identified Cheng's illness was by feeling his pulse: I detected a liver energy pattern.

sentences.zh: 肝氣濁而靜，此內關之病也。

translations.literal: Liver energy turbid yet quiet, this is an inner barrier illness.
translations.idiomatic: The liver energy was turbid yet still—this is the disease called Inner Obstruction.

sentences.zh: 脈法曰「脈長而弦，不得代四時者，其病主在於肝。

translations.literal: Pulse method say "pulse long yet string, not able dai four seasons, its illness main at liver.
translations.idiomatic: The pulse method says "pulse long and tense, unable to substitute for the four seasons, the illness mainly resides in the liver.

sentences.zh: 和即經主病也，代則絡脈有過」。

translations.literal: Harmony then classic main illness, dai then luo pulse have fault".
translations.idiomatic: Harmony then the classic governs the illness, substitution then the network vessels have fault."

sentences.zh: 經主病和者，其病得之筋髓里。

translations.literal: When the classic governs illness in harmony, the illness comes from the muscle marrow interior.
translations.idiomatic: When the primary channels govern a disease in its harmonious phase, the illness originates deep within the sinews and marrow.

sentences.zh: 其代絕而脈賁者，病得之酒且內。

translations.literal: When substitution breaks and pulse surges, illness comes from wine and sexual excess.
translations.idiomatic: When there is intermittent cessation and the pulse surges, the illness arises from drinking and sexual indulgence.

sentences.zh: 所以知其後五日而擁腫，八日嘔膿死者，切其脈時，少陽初代。

translations.literal: The reason I knew it would swell and gather after five days, vomit pus and die after eight days, when I cut his pulse, lesser yang initially substituted.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I knew the swelling would develop after five days and that he would vomit pus and die after eight was that when I felt his pulse, the Lesser Yang channel had just begun to show intermittent cessation.

sentences.zh: 代者經病，病去過人，人則去。

translations.literal: Substitution means classic illness, illness exceeds the person, person then dies.
translations.idiomatic: Intermittent cessation signifies a disease of the primary channels. When the disease overwhelms the patient, the patient dies.

sentences.zh: 絡脈主病，當其時，少陽初關一分，故中熱而膿未發也，及五分，則至少陽之界，及八日，則嘔膿死，故上二分而膿發，至界而擁腫，盡泄而死。

translations.literal: Network vessels govern illness, at that time, lesser yang initially closed one fen, therefore internally hot but pus not erupted, reaching five fen then to lesser yang's boundary, reaching eight days then vomits pus and dies, therefore ascending two fen and pus erupted, reaching boundary and swelling massed, fully discharged and died.
translations.idiomatic: The connecting vessels govern this disease. At that time, the Lesser Yang had just closed by one division, which is why there was internal heat but the pus had not yet formed. At five divisions it would reach the boundary of Lesser Yang, and after eight days he would vomit pus and die. Thus, at two divisions the pus erupted; at the boundary the swelling massed; and when the flow was fully discharged, he died.

sentences.zh: 熱上則熏陽明，爛流絡，流絡動則脈結發，脈結發則爛解，故絡交。

translations.literal: Heat ascending then steams the yang brightness, rotting flows the networks, flowing networks move then pulse knots erupt, pulse knots erupt then rot dissolves, therefore networks intersect.
translations.idiomatic: As the heat rose, it scorched the Yang Brightness channel, causing corruption to flow through the connecting vessels. When the corrupted connecting vessels were agitated, knotted eruptions formed in the pulse. Once these knotted eruptions burst, the corruption dissolved, and so the connecting vessels became entangled.

sentences.zh: 熱氣已上行，至頭而動，故頭痛。

translations.literal: Hot energy already ascended, reaching the head and moving, therefore headache.
translations.idiomatic: The hot energy had already risen upward, reaching the head and stirring there, which caused the headaches.

sentences.zh: 齊王中子諸嬰兒小子病，召臣意診切其脈，告曰：「氣鬲病。

translations.literal: The middle son of the King of Qi, Zhuying'er the young master, fell ill. The king summoned me to feel his pulse and I reported: "This is an illness of blocked qi at the diaphragm.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuying'er, a young son among the king of Qi's middle sons, took ill. The king summoned me to examine his pulse, and I reported: "This is diaphragmatic qi blockage.

sentences.zh: 病使人煩懣，食不下，時嘔沫。

translations.literal: The illness makes a person vexed and oppressed, unable to eat, sometimes vomiting foam.
translations.idiomatic: The illness caused the patient to feel agitated and suffocated, unable to keep food down, and at times he would vomit foam.

sentences.zh: 病得之（少）［心］憂，數忔食飲。」

translations.literal: The illness came from sorrow of heart and frequent sighing while eating and drinking."
translations.idiomatic: The disease arose from grief in the heart and repeated distress while eating and drinking."

sentences.zh: 臣意即為之作下氣湯以飲之，一日氣下，二日能食，三日即病愈。

translations.literal: Minister Yi then made descending energy soup for him to drink, one day energy descended, two days able to eat, three days then illness cured.
translations.idiomatic: I prepared a Descending Energy Decoction for him to drink. After one day the energy subsided, after two days he could eat again, and by the third day the illness was cured.

sentences.zh: 所以知小子之病者，診其脈，心氣也，濁躁而經也，此絡陽病也。

translations.literal: The reason I knew the young son's illness was diagnosing his pulse—heart energy, turbid and agitated yet classical, this is network yang illness.
translations.idiomatic: The way I identified the young man's illness was by reading his pulse—it revealed a heart energy pattern that was turbid and agitated yet still in the primary channel. This is the disease known as Connecting Yang.

sentences.zh: 脈法曰「脈來數疾去難而不一者，病主在心」。

translations.literal: The pulse canon says: "When the pulse comes rapidly and urgently and departs with difficulty and irregularity, the illness chiefly resides in the heart."
translations.idiomatic: The canon of pulse diagnosis states: "If the pulse arrives swiftly and urgently yet leaves with difficulty and without uniformity, the disease is governed by the heart."

sentences.zh: 周身熱，脈盛者，為重陽。

translations.literal: When the whole body is hot and the pulse is surging, this is Excess Yang.
translations.idiomatic: When heat fills the entire body and the pulse is full and rapid, the pattern is Excess Yang.

sentences.zh: 重陽者，逿心主。

translations.literal: Excess Yang means the heart is overwhelmed.
translations.idiomatic: Excess Yang indicates that the heart is overborne.

sentences.zh: 故煩懣食不下則絡脈有過，絡脈有過則血上出，血上出者死。

translations.literal: Therefore when there is vexation and food will not go down, the connecting vessels are diseased; when the connecting vessels are diseased, blood rises and is expelled; when blood rises and is expelled, the patient dies.
translations.idiomatic: Hence when agitation and inability to eat appear, the connecting vessels are at fault; when those vessels fail, blood surges upward and is lost—and when blood surges upward and is lost, death follows.

sentences.zh: 此悲心所生也，病得之憂也。

translations.literal: This arises from a sorrowful heart; the illness came from worry.
translations.idiomatic: Such conditions spring from grief in the heart; the disease was born of anxiety.

sentences.zh: 齊郎中令循病，眾醫皆以為蹙入中，而刺之。

translations.literal: Xun, the palace physician of Qi, fell ill; all the physicians thought the malady had entered the center and needled him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, director of the palace physicians in Qi, took ill. The other doctors all believed the disease had penetrated inward and treated him with acupuncture.

sentences.zh: 臣意診之，曰：「湧疝也，令人不得前後溲。」

translations.literal: I examined him and said: "This is a surging hernia; it prevents both urination and defecation."
translations.idiomatic: When I diagnosed him, I said: "This is surging hernia—it keeps him from passing urine or stool."

sentences.zh: 循曰：「不得前後溲三日矣。」

translations.literal: Xun said: "I have been unable to urinate or defecate for three days."
translations.idiomatic: Xun replied: "I have not been able to pass water or stool for three days now."

sentences.zh: 臣意飲以火齊湯，一飲得前［后］溲，再飲大溲，三飲而疾愈。

translations.literal: I had him drink a Fire Formula decoction; after one dose he could urinate again, after the second he had a full bowel movement, and after the third the illness was cured.
translations.idiomatic: I gave him the Fire Formula broth to drink. One dose restored urination, a second produced a full evacuation, and with the third the disease was gone.

sentences.zh: 病得之內。

translations.literal: The illness came from internal causes.
translations.idiomatic: The disease arose from an internal disorder.

sentences.zh: 所以知循病者，切其脈時，右口氣急，脈無五藏氣，右口脈大而數。

translations.literal: The reason I knew Xun's illness was when I cut his pulse, right mouth energy urgent, pulse without five viscera energies, right mouth pulse large and rapid.
translations.idiomatic: The way I identified Xun's illness was that when I felt his pulse, the energy at the right wrist was urgent, the pulse showed no response from the five organs, and the right wrist pulse was large and rapid.

sentences.zh: 數者中下熱而湧，左為下，右為上，皆無五藏應，故曰湧疝。

translations.literal: Rapid means middle and lower hot and surging, left is lower, right is upper, all without five viscera response, therefore called surging hernia.
translations.idiomatic: A rapid pulse indicates heat in the middle and lower regions with surging energy—the left pulse corresponds to the lower body, the right to the upper. Since neither showed any response from the five organs, the diagnosis was Surging Hernia.

sentences.zh: 中熱，故溺赤也。

translations.literal: Internal heat, therefore urine red.
translations.idiomatic: The internal heat caused the urine to turn red.

sentences.zh: 齊中御府長信病，臣意入診其脈，告曰：「熱病氣也。

translations.literal: Changxin, director of the central imperial storehouse in Qi, fell ill. I entered, felt his pulse, and reported: "This is an illness of heat affecting the qi.
translations.idiomatic: Changxin, overseer of the central imperial wardrobe in Qi, was ill. I went in, examined his pulse, and told him: "This is heat disease affecting the qi.

sentences.zh: 然暑汗，脈少衰，不死。」

translations.literal: Yet he is sweating from summer heat and the pulse is slightly weakened; he will not die."
translations.idiomatic: Still, because he is perspiring from the summer heat, the pulse is somewhat depleted—he will not die."

sentences.zh: 曰：「此病得之當浴流水而寒甚，已則熱。」

translations.literal: I said: "This illness came from bathing in running water when the cold was severe; afterward heat developed."
translations.idiomatic: I told him: "You contracted this by bathing in flowing water during intense cold; once that passed, fever set in."

sentences.zh: 信曰：「唯，然！

translations.literal: Xin said: "Wei, ran!
translations.idiomatic: Xin said: "Yes, indeed!

sentences.zh: 往冬時，為王使於楚，至莒縣陽周水，而莒橋梁頗壞，信則擥車轅未欲渡也，馬驚，即墮，信身入水中，幾死，吏即來救信，出之水中，衣盡濡，有閒而身寒，已熱如火，至今不可以見寒。」

translations.literal: Last winter, when I was the king's envoy to Chu, I reached the Yangzhou waters in Ju county. The bridge piers at Ju were badly damaged. I gripped the carriage shaft, not yet willing to cross, when the horse took fright and fell. I plunged into the water and nearly died. Officials came at once and pulled me out; my clothes were soaked through. After a while I felt cold through the body, then suddenly burned hot as fire, and from that time I cannot bear cold."
translations.idiomatic: In the winter past, while serving as the king's envoy to Chu, I came to the Yangzhou ford in Ju county. The bridge there was badly broken. I was holding the carriage pole, hesitating to cross, when the horse shied and fell. I was thrown into the water and nearly drowned. Officers rescued me at once and drew me out, drenched to the skin. Shortly afterward a chill ran through me, then heat blazed up like fire, and since then I cannot endure cold."

sentences.zh: 臣意即為之液湯火齊逐熱，一飲汗盡，再飲熱去，三飲病已。

translations.literal: Minister Yi then made fluid soup fire elixir to expel heat for him, one drink sweat completely, second drink heat gone, third drink illness cured.
translations.idiomatic: I then prepared a Liquid Decoction with a Fire Formula to drive out the heat. After one dose, the sweating ceased entirely; after the second, the heat subsided; and after the third, the illness was cured.

sentences.zh: 即使服藥，出入二十日，身無病者。

translations.literal: Then had him take medicine, coming and going twenty days, body without illness.
translations.idiomatic: I then had him continue taking medicine, and after roughly twenty days of treatment, his body was free of illness.

sentences.zh: 所以知信之病者，切其脈時，并陰。

translations.literal: The reason I knew Xin's illness was when I cut his pulse, parallel yin.
translations.idiomatic: The way I identified Xin's illness was that when I felt his pulse, I found Concurrent Yin.

sentences.zh: 脈法曰「熱病陰陽交者死」。

translations.literal: The pulse canon says: "In heat disease, when yin and yang intersect, the patient dies."
translations.idiomatic: The canon states: "In febrile disease, if yin and yang cross and bind, the patient dies."

sentences.zh: 切之不交，并陰。

translations.literal: Cut it not intersecting, parallel yin.
translations.idiomatic: When I felt the pulse, it did not alternate—it was Concurrent Yin.

sentences.zh: 并陰者，脈順清而愈，其熱雖未盡，猶活也。

translations.literal: Parallel yin means pulse smooth clear and cured, its heat though not exhausted, still lives.
translations.idiomatic: In the case of Concurrent Yin, the pulse runs smooth and clear, and recovery follows. Though the heat may not have fully dissipated, the patient will survive.

sentences.zh: 腎氣有時閒濁，在太陰脈口而希，是水氣也。

translations.literal: Kidney energy sometimes clear turbid, at taiyin pulse mouth and sparse, this is water energy.
translations.idiomatic: The kidney energy was at times intermittently turbid, appearing at the Taiyin pulse point but sparse—this indicated a condition of Water Energy.

sentences.zh: 腎固主水，故以此知之。

translations.literal: Kidney firmly governs water, therefore with this know it.
translations.idiomatic: Since the kidneys inherently govern water, I was able to identify the condition from this.

sentences.zh: 失治一時，即轉為寒熱。

translations.literal: Lose treatment one time, then turns to cold heat.
translations.idiomatic: If treatment were missed even once, the condition would turn into alternating chills and fever.

sentences.zh: 齊王太后病，召臣意入診脈，曰：「風癉客脬，難於大小溲，溺赤。」

translations.literal: The queen dowager of Qi fell ill. The king summoned me to feel her pulse, and I said: "Wind obstruction has lodged in the bladder, making both great and small urination difficult; the urine is red."
translations.idiomatic: The queen mother of Qi took ill. The king called me to examine her pulse, and I said: "Wind-damp has settled in the bladder, so both kinds of urination are hard, and the urine is red."

sentences.zh: 臣意飲以火齊湯，一飲即前後溲，再飲病已，溺如故。

translations.literal: I had her drink the Fire Formula decoction; after one dose she could urinate freely, after the second the illness was gone, and her urine returned to normal.
translations.idiomatic: I gave her the Fire Formula broth. One dose restored urination front and back; with the second the disease ended and her urine was normal again.

sentences.zh: 病得之流汗出循。

translations.literal: The illness came from sweating while the body was exposed.
translations.idiomatic: She contracted it by sweating and then letting the wind strike her bare skin.

sentences.zh: 循者，去衣而汗晞也。

translations.literal: "Xun" means to strip off clothing and let the sweat dry in the air.
translations.idiomatic: "Xun" means to remove one's garments and allow the perspiration to dry upon the skin.

sentences.zh: 所以知齊王太后病者，臣意診其脈，切其太陰之口，溼然風氣也。

translations.literal: The reason I knew the queen mother of Qi's illness was that when I examined her pulse and felt the Taiyin opening, there was a moist wind pattern.
translations.idiomatic: I recognized the queen mother's disease because, on examining her pulse at the Taiyin position, I found a damp, windlike quality.

sentences.zh: 脈法曰「沈之而大堅，浮之而大緊者，病主在腎」。

translations.literal: The pulse canon says: "When pressed deeply it is large and firm; when felt superficially it is large and tight—the illness chiefly resides in the kidneys."
translations.idiomatic: The canon of pulse diagnosis states: "If sinking brings a large, firm pulse and floating brings a large, tight one, the disease is governed by the kidneys."

sentences.zh: 腎切之而相反也，脈大而躁。

translations.literal: When the kidney pulse is cut and runs contrary, the pulse is large and agitated.
translations.idiomatic: When one feels the kidney pulse and finds it running counter to the norm, it is large and restless.

sentences.zh: 大者，膀胱氣也；

translations.literal: Large means bladder qi;
translations.idiomatic: A large pulse indicates qi of the bladder;

sentences.zh: 躁者，中有熱而溺赤。

translations.literal: agitated means heat within and red urine.
translations.idiomatic: agitation means internal heat with red urine.

sentences.zh: 齊章武里曹山跗病，臣意診其脈，曰：「肺消癉也，加以寒熱。」

translations.literal: Cao Shanfu of Zhangwu Lane in Qi fell ill. I felt his pulse and said: "Lung wasting with seizure, complicated by alternating cold and heat."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shanfu of Zhangwu Lane in Qi took ill. I examined his pulse and said: "This is pulmonary consumption with convulsive illness, aggravated by chills and fever."

sentences.zh: 即告其人曰：「死，不治。

translations.literal: Then tell his person said: "Die, not treat.
translations.idiomatic: Then he told his family: "He will die, cannot be treated.

sentences.zh: 適其共養，此不當醫治。」

translations.literal: Attend to his shared care—this is not a case for medical treatment."
translations.idiomatic: See to his maintenance in common; this should not be treated as a medical matter."

sentences.zh: 法曰「後三日而當狂，妄起行，欲走；

translations.literal: Law say "after three days yet should mad, wild rise walk, desire run;
translations.idiomatic: The law says "after three days he will certainly go mad, wildly rise and walk, wanting to run;

sentences.zh: 後五日死」。

translations.literal: after five days die".
translations.idiomatic: He will die within five days."

sentences.zh: 即如期死。

translations.literal: Then he died as predicted.
translations.idiomatic: He died precisely on schedule.

sentences.zh: 山跗病得之盛怒而以接內。

translations.literal: Shanfu's illness came from extreme anger combined with sexual excess.
translations.idiomatic: Shanfu's illness arose from extreme anger combined with sexual indulgence.

sentences.zh: 所以知山跗之病者，臣意切其脈，肺氣熱也。

translations.literal: The reason I knew Shanfu's illness was that Minister Yi cut his pulse—lung energy hot.
translations.idiomatic: The way I identified Shanfu's illness was by feeling his pulse—the lung energy was hot.

sentences.zh: 脈法曰「不平不鼓，形獘」。

translations.literal: Pulse law say "not level not gu, form bie".
translations.idiomatic: The pulse law says "not level not drumming, form withered".

sentences.zh: 此五藏高之遠數以經病也，故切之時不平而代。

translations.literal: This is five viscera elevated distant numbering with classic illness, therefore when cut not level but substitution.
translations.idiomatic: This was a case where the five organs had grown elevated, causing a distant and rapid pulse pattern associated with a disease of the primary channels. Therefore, when I felt the pulse, it was irregular with intermittent cessations.

sentences.zh: 不平者，血不居其處；

translations.literal: Not level person, blood not live its place;
translations.idiomatic: Not level means blood does not reside in its place;

sentences.zh: 代者，時參擊并至，乍躁乍大也。

translations.literal: Substitution means times strike together arriving, suddenly agitated suddenly large.
translations.idiomatic: Intermittent cessation in this case meant that at times the pulses struck in clusters, arriving together—now agitated, now surging.

sentences.zh: 此兩絡脈絕，故死不治。

translations.literal: These two network vessels severed, therefore dies cannot be treated.
translations.idiomatic: Both of these connecting vessels had been severed, and so the patient died—the case was beyond treatment.

sentences.zh: 所以加寒熱者，言其人尸奪。

translations.literal: The reason for adding alternating cold and heat is that the person has corpse deprivation.
translations.idiomatic: The reason his condition worsened into alternating chills and fever was that his body had been seized by a Corpse Deprivation syndrome.

sentences.zh: 尸奪者，形獘；

translations.literal: Shi duo person, form bie;
translations.idiomatic: Corpse deprivation means form withered;

sentences.zh: 形獘者，不當關灸鑱石及飲毒藥也。

translations.literal: Form withered means should not apply moxibustion, needles and stones, nor drink poisonous medicines.
translations.idiomatic: When the body is so wasted, one should not apply moxibustion, acupuncture, or mineral remedies, nor administer strong medicines.

sentences.zh: 臣意未往診時，齊太醫先診山跗病，灸其足少陽脈口，而飲之半夏丸，病者即泄注，腹中虛；

translations.literal: Before I had gone to examine him, the chief physician of Qi had already diagnosed Shanfu's illness, cauterized the opening of the shaoyang pulse on his foot, and given him Banxia pills. The patient at once suffered diarrhea and leakage, and his abdomen was depleted within.
translations.idiomatic: Before I was called in, Qi's chief physician had already treated Shanfu, moxibusting the shaoyang point on his foot and administering Banxia pills. The man immediately developed pouring diarrhea, and his middle abdomen was left empty.

sentences.zh: 又灸其少陰脈，是壞肝剛絕深，如是重損病者氣，以故加寒熱。

translations.literal: Again moxibusted his shaoyin pulse, this damaged the liver tendon and severed deeply, like this heavily damaged the ill person's energy, for this reason added alternating cold and heat.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, they applied moxibustion to his Shaoyin channel, which damaged the liver's tendon connection and severed it deep within. This inflicted severe harm on the patient's vital energy, which is why the alternating chills and fever worsened.

sentences.zh: 所以後三日而當狂者，肝一絡連屬結絕乳下陽明，故絡絕，開陽明脈，陽明脈傷，即當狂走。

translations.literal: The reason after three days he would certainly go mad is that the liver's one network connects and belongs, knot severed below the nipple yangming, therefore network severed, opens the yangming vessel, yangming vessel injured, then would certainly madly run.
translations.idiomatic: The reason he would go mad after three days was that one of the liver's connecting vessels links to and ties off at the Yang Brightness channel below the nipple. When this connecting vessel was severed, it opened a pathway into the Yang Brightness channel. Once the Yang Brightness channel was injured, the patient would inevitably run about in a frenzy.

sentences.zh: 後五日死者，肝與心相去五分，故曰五日盡，盡即死矣。

translations.literal: The reason after five days he dies is that liver and heart are mutually five fen apart, therefore called five days exhausted, exhausted then dies.
translations.idiomatic: The reason he would die after five days was that the liver and the heart are separated by five divisions. Therefore I said that in five days the energy would be exhausted, and once exhausted, he would die.

sentences.zh: 齊中尉潘滿如病少腹痛，臣意診其脈，曰：「遺積瘕也。」

translations.literal: Pan Manru, a commandant of Qi, suffered pain in the lower abdomen. I felt his pulse and said: "Retained accumulation and abdominal mass."
translations.idiomatic: Pan Manru, a commandant in Qi, was afflicted with pain in the lower belly. On reading his pulse I said: "This is stagnant accumulation forming a mass."

sentences.zh: 臣意即謂齊太仆臣饒、內史臣繇曰：「中尉不復自止於內，則三十日死。」

translations.literal: I then told the Grand Coachman Rao and the Interior Minister You of Qi: "If the commandant cannot again restrain himself internally, he will die in thirty days."
translations.idiomatic: I at once informed Grand Coachman Rao and Interior Minister You: "Unless the commandant can once more control himself inwardly, he will be dead within thirty days."

sentences.zh: 後二十餘日，溲血死。

translations.literal: After over twenty days, urinated blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: After more than twenty days, he passed blood in his urine and died.

sentences.zh: 病得之酒且內。

translations.literal: Illness came from wine and sexual excess.
translations.idiomatic: The illness arose from excessive drinking and sexual indulgence.

sentences.zh: 所以知潘滿如病者，臣意切其脈深小弱，其卒然合合也，是脾氣也。

translations.literal: The reason I knew Pan Manru's illness was that Minister Yi cut his pulse deep small weak, its suddenly contracting contracting, this is spleen energy.
translations.idiomatic: The way I identified Pan Manru's illness was by feeling his pulse: it was deep, small, and weak, contracting abruptly in a clenching pattern—this was a sign of spleen energy.

sentences.zh: 右脈口氣至緊小，見瘕氣也。

translations.literal: Right pulse mouth energy reaches tight small, sees abdominal mass energy.
translations.idiomatic: The energy at the right wrist pulse was extremely tight and small, revealing the presence of an abdominal mass.

sentences.zh: 以次相乘，故三十日死。

translations.literal: Multiplying in order by order, therefore dies in thirty days.
translations.idiomatic: With each organ being overwhelmed by the next in succession, death would come in thirty days.

sentences.zh: 三陰俱摶者，如法；

translations.literal: Three yin all tuan person, like law;
translations.idiomatic: Three yin all knotted means, like the law;

sentences.zh: 不俱摶者，決在急期；

translations.literal: When the pulse is not uniformly knotted, the decision falls in the urgent period;
translations.idiomatic: When the pulse is not fully bound, the outcome is decided within the critical interval;

sentences.zh: 一摶一代者，近也。

translations.literal: One knotted one substituted means, near.
translations.idiomatic: When the pulse alternates between one knotted beat and one skipped beat, death is near.

sentences.zh: 故其三陰摶，溲血如前止。

translations.literal: Therefore his three yin knotted, urinated blood like before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, when all three yin pulses became knotted, the blood in the urine ceased just as before.

sentences.zh: 陽虛侯相趙章病，召臣意。

translations.literal: Yangxu Marquis Chancellor Zhao Zhang fell ill, summoned Minister Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhang, the chancellor of the Marquis of Yangxu, fell ill and summoned me.

sentences.zh: 眾醫皆以為寒中，臣意診其脈曰：「迵風。」

translations.literal: All the physicians regarded it as cold striking the center. I felt his pulse and said: "Straight wind."
translations.idiomatic: The other doctors all diagnosed cold penetrating inward. I examined his pulse and said: "Direct wind."

sentences.zh: 迵風者，飲食下嗌而輒出不留。

translations.literal: Straight wind means food and drink descend the throat but immediately exit without staying.
translations.idiomatic: Penetrating Wind is a condition in which food and drink pass down the throat but are immediately expelled, unable to remain in the body.

sentences.zh: 法曰「五日死」，而後十日乃死。

translations.literal: Law say "five days die", yet after ten days then die.
translations.idiomatic: The law says "five days die", but after ten days then died.

sentences.zh: 病得之酒。

translations.literal: Illness came from wine.
translations.idiomatic: The illness arose from excessive drinking.

sentences.zh: 所以知趙章之病者，臣意切其脈，脈來滑，是內風氣也。

translations.literal: The reason I knew Zhao Zhang's illness was that Minister Yi cut his pulse, pulse came slippery, this is internal wind energy.
translations.idiomatic: The way I identified Zhao Zhang's illness was by feeling his pulse: it came slippery, indicating internal Wind Energy.

sentences.zh: 飲食下嗌而輒出不留者，法五日死，皆為前分界法。

translations.literal: Food and drink descend throat but immediately exit without staying means, law five days die, all become the front boundary demarcation law.
translations.idiomatic: When food and drink pass down the throat but are immediately expelled and cannot be retained, the standard prognosis is death within five days—this follows the method of boundary demarcation.

sentences.zh: 後十日乃死，所以過期者，其人嗜粥，故中藏實，中藏實故過期。

translations.literal: After ten days then died, the reason exceeded the period is that the person liked congee, therefore middle viscera solid, middle viscera solid therefore exceeded period.
translations.idiomatic: He did not die until ten days had passed. The reason he outlived the prediction was that he was fond of congee, which kept his internal organs nourished. Because his organs remained nourished, he exceeded the expected time.

sentences.zh: 師言曰「安穀者過期，不安穀者不及期」。

translations.literal: Shi speak say "An gu person exceed period, not an gu person not reach period".
translations.idiomatic: The master said "Those who settle grain exceed the period, those who do not settle grain do not reach the period".

sentences.zh: 濟北王病，召臣意診其脈，曰：「風蹶胸滿。」

translations.literal: The king of Jibei fell ill and summoned me to feel his pulse. I said: "Wind reversal with fullness in the chest."
translations.idiomatic: When the king of Jibei took ill, he called me to examine his pulse. I reported: "Wind reversal with oppression in the chest."

sentences.zh: 即為藥酒，盡三石，病已。

translations.literal: Then made medicinal wine, drank three dan completely, illness cured.
translations.idiomatic: I prepared a medicinal wine for him, and after he had consumed three dan of it, his illness was cured.

sentences.zh: 得之汗出伏地。

translations.literal: Got it from sweating out prostrate on ground.
translations.idiomatic: He contracted the illness from sweating while lying face down on the ground.

sentences.zh: 所以知濟北王病者，臣意切其脈時，風氣也，心脈濁。

translations.literal: The reason I knew Jibei King's illness was that Minister Yi cut his pulse, wind energy, heart pulse turbid.
translations.idiomatic: The way I identified the King of Jibei's illness was that when I felt his pulse, I found a Wind Energy pattern and the heart pulse was turbid.

sentences.zh: 病法「過入其陽，陽氣盡而陰氣入」。

translations.literal: Illness law "guo enter its yang, yang qi jin yet yin qi enter".
translations.idiomatic: Illness law "excess enters its yang, yang energy exhausted then yin energy enters".

sentences.zh: 陰氣入張，則寒氣上而熱氣下，故胸滿。

translations.literal: Yin energy enters and expands, then cold energy ascends and hot energy descends, therefore chest fullness.
translations.idiomatic: When yin energy enters and expands, cold energy rises while hot energy sinks, which causes a sensation of fullness in the chest.

sentences.zh: 汗出伏地者，切其脈，氣陰。

translations.literal: Sweating out prostrate on ground means, cut his pulse, energy yin.
translations.idiomatic: That the illness came from sweating while prostrate on the ground was confirmed when I felt his pulse—the energy was yin.

sentences.zh: 陰氣者，病必入中，出及瀺水也。

translations.literal: Yin energy means illness must enter center, exit reaches dribbling water.
translations.idiomatic: When yin energy predominates, the illness inevitably penetrates deep into the body's interior and manifests outwardly as dribbling urine.

sentences.zh: 齊北宮司空命婦出於病，眾醫皆以為風入中，病主在肺，刺其足少陽脈。

translations.literal: Qi northern palace overseer's wife fell ill, all doctors considered wind entered center, illness mainly at lung, stabbed her foot shaoyang vessel.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of the Director of Works at the Northern Palace in Qi developed a prolapse condition. The other physicians all believed that wind had entered the body and that the disease was centered in the lungs, so they needled her Foot Shaoyang channel.

sentences.zh: 臣意診其脈，曰：「病氣疝，客於膀胱，難於前後溲，而溺赤。

translations.literal: I felt her pulse and said: "Qi hernia illness, lodging in the bladder, making both kinds of urination difficult, and the urine is red.
translations.idiomatic: On examining her pulse I said: "This is qi hernia. It has settled in the bladder, so both great and small urination are difficult, and the urine is red.

sentences.zh: 病見寒氣則遺溺，使人腹腫。」

translations.literal: When the illness meets cold qi, there is incontinence, and the abdomen swells."
translations.idiomatic: When cold influences strike the disease, she cannot retain urine, and the belly distends."

sentences.zh: 出於病得之欲溺不得，因以接內。

translations.literal: Protruding illness comes from wanting to urinate but unable, thus with sexual excess.
translations.idiomatic: The prolapse condition arose from being unable to urinate despite the urge, compounded by sexual indulgence.

sentences.zh: 所以知出於病者，切其脈大而實，其來難，是蹶陰之動也。

translations.literal: The reason I knew protruding illness was cutting his pulse large and substantial, its coming difficult, this is jueyin's movement.
